cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the fallen tent for a moment. Remember the loose peg I pointed out? This is the turning point I was preparing you for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were supposed to hammer it in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'd have missed what that little warning meant. Look at the whole roof now; you can see why I singled it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see we're getting soaked. Can we put it back up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Start with that peg, and I'll tell you when it's deep enough. We needed the roof down before everyone understood the opening warning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders a pause and claims peg warning prepared the fall; A3 directs attention to roof as planned revelation; A5 grants rebuilding and supervises peg depth while claiming the fall was necessary.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 neglected repair as deliberate preservation of warning significance; A5 uses B4 rain and rebuild request to make repair the next planned step.

relationship.evidence: B2 holds A to repair duty and B4 seeks shelter, plausible practical urgency.

heightening.evidence: A5 returns to B4 rebuilding through the same peg and claims collapse completed the earlier warning, avoiding a new coat callback.
